text:
aneesh: quick heads-up — noticed a recurring latency tail when streaming with continuous batching and small token budgets (esp <64). attaching profiler snippet below. anyone seen this pattern?

maria: yep, saw it this morning on canary. looks like partial-decode tasks are delaying stream flushes. 

kevin: interesting — is this the k-select v2 rollout? I saw a perf bump on long sequences but regressions on short ones.

aneesh: looks correlated. profiler:```
profile summary:
 kernel_select: 11.8ms
 kv_cache_lookup: 1.9ms
 batch_wait_queue: 42.6ms
 partial_decode: 27.2ms
 stream_flush_wait: 65.1ms
 total_p50: 88ms
 total_p95: 320ms
```

sasha: stream_flush_wait >> partial_decode; suspect scheduling order. continuous batcher currently favours filling by token budget then dispatching partial-decode as worker availability allows. for streaming we probably want a low-latency preempt path.

oliver: +1. two levers: (1) flush cadence timer (force flush at X ms even if budget not full) (2) partial-decode prioritization: let partial-decode run immediately for streams and preempt long non-stream decodes.

maria: tried a local tweak: set token_budget_target=32 for streaming route and added a 35ms flush timeout. p95 dropped ~70ms on canary. downside: small increase in overall tokens per request because less batching.

kevin: do we have any kernel selection effects? small batches choose the fallback kernel that’s slower per-token. maybe force kernel_hint=low_latency for streams.

aneesh: good call. there's also KV cache contention on worker threads when partial-decode touches older KV shards — we should pin stream requests to workers with warm KV and prefer lightweight KV path.

runtime-bot: deploy v2.14.3 started by @kevin — rollout steps: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> all. observability flag 'streaming_lowlat' enabled only in canary.

oliver: action plan:
 - kevin: add kernel_hint override for streaming routes (low_latency) and add test in perf harness.
 - sasha: prototype preemptive scheduler: partial-decode-first for streaming request types. include fairness cap to avoid starving long batch jobs.
 - maria: run a/b with token_budget_target 32 vs 48 and flush_timer 35ms vs 50ms. capture token-efficiency and p95.
 - aneesh: add KV warm-worker affinity flag for streams and gather KV hot-count metrics.

maria: I'll run canary tomorrow morning. quick note: set flush timer too low and we lose batching benefits — tradeoff sweet spot seems 30-45ms on our infra.

kevin: also logging idea: emit scheduling_reason in trace for every flush (budget/full_timer/preempt/kernel_switch) so we can query what actually triggered sends in prod.

aneesh: love that. if we can attribute regressions to scheduling_reason we can roll back targeted knobs faster.

sasha: I'll sketch the scheduler changes and post a mini-PR with benchmark harness. expecting ~15% p95 improvement for streams if we get partial-decode prioritized and kernel_hint applied.

kevin: heads-up: kernel_hint might need a small fallback in case low_latency kernel OOMs on some GPUs. add fallback path.

maria: noted. will include fallback metric. thanks folks.

aneesh: great sync. tagging this thread for follow-ups. :)
